summary: During a record snowstorm near Lake Tahoe, Google Maps routed drivers off closed highways onto remote, unmaintained mountain roads. Some drivers were stranded or turned back, and officials warned about relying too heavily on GPS.
technical_summary: A consumer navigation service rerouted traffic around highway closures onto seasonal or poorly maintained forest roads. Routing did not reliably account for seasonal closures or treacherous terrain, and many drivers followed the same suggested detour.

summary: A Lion Air Boeing 737 MAX crashed into the Java Sea, killing all 189 people aboard. Investigators found a faulty sensor repeatedly triggered an automated anti-stall system that forced the nose down while pilots struggled to regain control.
technical_summary: Boeing's MCAS flight-control software relied on a single angle-of-attack sensor that gave false readings, repeatedly commanding nose-down trim. Pilots were not clearly told about the system or how it differed from older 737s, and the faulty sensor had not been repaired.

summary: Amazon built an experimental AI tool to score job applicants, but it learned to favor men and downgrade resumes mentioning women's activities or women's colleges. Amazon abandoned the project and says recruiters never relied on it alone.
technical_summary: A machine-learning resume scorer rated candidates one to five stars, trained on about ten years of submitted resumes that were mostly from men. It learned to penalize terms such as "women's"; edits to neutralize terms could not guarantee fairness, and the project was scrapped.

summary: Analyses of the Stable Diffusion image generator found it produced gender and racial stereotypes for job and crime prompts, often more extreme than real-world statistics. Women and people with darker skin were underrepresented for high-paying jobs.
technical_summary: A text-to-image diffusion model trained on web-scale data amplified demographic disparities: prompts such as engineer, judge or CEO yielded mostly men, while low-paying jobs and crime terms skewed toward darker-skinned people. Researchers measured the disparities across thousands of generated images.

summary: A newspaper investigation found LinkedIn's search suggested male names when users searched for common female names, but not the reverse. LinkedIn denied bias, saying results reflect past search behavior, and updated the algorithm to stop proposing alternative names.
technical_summary: LinkedIn's search suggestion feature ranked similar-spelling names using relative frequencies in past queries and member profiles. This produced prompts such as swapping female first names for male ones, a pattern absent for male names, until a fix recognized names explicitly.
